title: Biocompatibility of Veratric Acid-Encapsulated Chitosan/Methylcellulose Hydrogel: Biological Characterization, Osteogenic Efficiency with In Silico Molecular Modeling.
authors: Durairaj, Kaliannan; Balasubramanian, Balamuralikrishnan; Arumugam, Vijaya Anand; Easwaran, Murugesh; Park, Sungkwon; Issara, Utthapon; Pushparaj, Karthika; Al-Dhabi, Naif Abdullah; Arasu, Mariadhas Valan; Liu, Wen-Chao; Mousavi Khaneghah, Amin
one_liner_zh: 该文研究壳聚糖/甲基纤维素水凝胶包载藜芦酸用于骨修复，含VA与Runx2转录因子的分子对接，但核心是材料生物相容性与成骨分化，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI或MD模拟方法，仅边缘相关。
abstract: The limitations of graft material, and surgical sites for autografts in bone defects treatment have become a significant challenge in bone tissue engineering. Phytocompounds markedly affect bone metabolism by activating the osteogenic signaling pathways. The present study investigated the biocompatibility of the bio-composite thermo-responsive hydrogels consisting of chitosan (CS), and methylcellulose (MC) encapsulated with veratric acid (VA) as a restorative agent for bone defect treatment. The spectroscopy analyses confirmed the formation of CS/MC hydrogels and VA encapsulated CS/MC hydrogels (CS/MC-VA). Molecular analysis of the CS-specific MC decamer unit with VA complex exhibited a stable integration in the system. Further, Runx2 (runt-related transcription factor 2) was found in the docking mechanism with VA, indicating a high binding affinity towards the functional site of the Runx2 protein. The formulated CS/MC-VA hydrogels exhibited biocompatibility with the mouse mesenchymal stem cells, while VA promoted osteogenic differentiation in the stem cells, which was verified by calcium phosphate deposition through the von Kossa staining. The study results suggest that CS/MC-VA could be a potential therapeutic alternative source for bone regeneration.
abstract_zh: 骨缺损治疗中移植材料的局限性以及自体移植手术部位的问题，已成为骨组织工程中的重大挑战。植物化合物通过激活成骨信号通路显著影响骨代谢。本研究探讨了由壳聚糖（CS）和甲基纤维素（MC）组成的生物复合温敏水凝胶，并封装藜芦酸（VA）作为骨缺损治疗修复剂的生物相容性。光谱分析确认了CS/MC水凝胶及VA封装CS/MC水凝胶（CS/MC-VA）的形成。CS特异性MC十聚体单元与VA复合物的分子分析显示其在系统中稳定整合。此外，Runx2（runt相关转录因子2）在与VA的对接机制中被发现，表明其对Runx2蛋白功能位点具有高结合亲和力。所制备的CS/MC-VA水凝胶对小鼠间充质干细胞表现出生物相容性，而VA促进了干细胞的成骨分化，这通过von Kossa染色验证的磷酸钙沉积得以证实。研究结果表明，CS/MC-VA可能成为骨再生的潜在治疗替代来源。
